questions.question: Which scientist made the first observations on platinum as a catalyst and discovered similar triads of elements which led to the development of the Periodic Table of elements?

• The Periodic Table of **Elements** was developed as a result of **Johann** Wolfgang **Dobereiner's** discovery of comparable triads of elements and his first observation of** Platinum** as a catalyst.
 
• **Families** of **elements** with related **chemical characteristics** were first identified by Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner in **1829**.
 
• He **dubbed** these families **triads** because they always seemed to contain **three components**.
 
• One of these triads is represented by each of **Table 7.1's** vertical **columns**.

• All known **elements** are **organized **into **groups** on the **periodic table** based on characteristics. 
 
• As a result, **chemists**, nanotechnologists, and other** scientists** find it to be a **valuable tool**. 
 
• You can forecast how chemicals will react if you learn to use the periodic table and **comprehend** how it works. 
 
• The periodic table is a rapid reference tool used by scientists to look up details about an **element**, such as its atomic mass and **chemical symbol**. 
 
• The **arrangement** of the elements in the periodic table also enables scientists to identify **patterns** in the **electronegativity**, ionization energy, and **atomic radius **of the elements.
